newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat to higher.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond secondary prices opened flat to slightly higher Tuesday, while some big deals--including $250 million San Diego, Calif., Public Facilities Financing Authority bonds--got the primary market rolling early.
"The bid side might be 1/8 of a point better, but currently there is nothing going on yet," one trader said. "I don't think there's been a trade or anything like that."
A second trader largely concurred, describing the market as "absolutely dead quiet."
"Yesterday was a dead day, today's dead, there's just nothing to move the market in either direction really, or to change the tone," he said.
While Wednesday's first leg of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony may lend some direction, a trader said he doubted the Senate address would hold any surprises.
The House Banking Committee postponed the second leg of Greenspan's testimony to March 5 from Thursday because the date conflicted with a joint session of Congress.
Back in municipals, players are waiting to see how this week's new issues fare. Some $3.5 billion of fresh competitive and negotiated debt is expected.
"I think it will help," one trader said. "I don't think the market is scared of any supply, especially decent structure supply."
A second trader said players are looking to see how the new supply is received before making any further moves in the secondary, "so the market ends up a little bit quiet," he said.
Tuesday's new issues included the $250 million San Diego sewer revenue bonds via Smith Barney Inc. Preliminary pricing reflected a top yield of 5.61 percent in 2027.
Smith Barney also tentatively priced $155 million of Platte River Power Authority, Colo., power revenue bonds with a top yield of 5.50 percent in 2018.
Lehman Brothers tentatively priced $224 million Jacksonville Electric Authority, Fla., bonds at a top yield of 5.50 percent in 2016.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was up 9/32 at 117-7/32. The March T-bond contract was up 8/32 at 112-28/32. The MOB spread was 139 ticks.
The U.S. government market's 30-year bond was up 7/32 at 99-26/32 to yield 6.64 percent. The Treasury is slated to sell $17.5 billion of two-year notes today.
